title: The Odyssey
subtitle: The Long Way Home
attribution: An original abridged adaptation of Homer’s Odyssey
description: Ithaca receives a stranger before it recognizes its king.
intro: He has reached home. Home does not know him yet.
ending: Father and son had found one another. The house still waited.
stageLabel: A pixel art retelling of the Odyssey

adaptationSource.title: Homer, Odyssey, Books XIII–XVI
adaptationSource.note: Original abridged English narration and dialogue. Events are condensed for quiet episodic reading. Ritual sacrifice and deaths are represented without gore. The final conflict of Book XXIV is condensed to Athena intervening before renewed bloodshed.

steps.text: As Alcinous promised, a Phaeacian crew took Odysseus aboard. They sailed from Scheria toward Ithaca with gifts for their guest.
This time, other sailors guided the ship. Odysseus could sleep while they carried him home.

steps.text: Alcinous’s sailors brought the sleeping Odysseus ashore on Ithaca and left gifts beside him. Their ship then returned to Scheria.
He stood on his own island without knowing it. Even arrival could feel like another wrong turn.
Athena came to meet him. She named the place he had reached.
“Ithaca. You are home.”
He bent toward the ground. The journey had ended here once in his imagination; now the earth was real.
Athena concealed the gifts for safekeeping. He would have time to return for them when his house was safe.
“Then let me go to my house.”
“First, let us keep you alive long enough to enter it.”
Athena explained that the suitors still wanted his wife and his throne. They might attack him if they knew he was home.
“A king would draw their eyes. A beggar may hear what they say.”
His dark hair greyed. His clothes became patched and worn. The man in the sand looked old enough to be overlooked.
“Follow the path to Eumaeus, the man who cares for your pigs. He is still loyal to you,” Athena said.
“Will he know me?”
“Let him welcome you without knowing.”
Odysseus followed the path inland, carrying a stranger’s face into the country he had missed.

steps.text: The path led to Eumaeus’s hut and pig pens. Eumaeus saw an old traveler; he did not know that the man was his king.
“Come in from the road. There is bread.”
He set bread on the table. He asked no payment and waited for no impressive name.
“You have a generous master.”
“I had one. The sea has kept him too long.”
Odysseus looked down at the bread. His own servant had offered a stranger what the suitors would not share.
He listened to news of his household without saying that it was his.
Telemachus had left Sparta and sailed back to Ithaca. He came to the trusted swineherd before going to the palace.
Telemachus returned from his search and came first to Eumaeus. The swineherd looked up to greet him.
“You are back. Let your mother hear it before another rumor reaches her.”
The young man glanced toward the stranger. Odysseus saw the child he remembered in a face almost grown.
“He may stay here. See that he has what he needs.”
His father said nothing. It was the first kindness his son had given him, without knowing who received it.

eumaeus.zone: Path from the hut toward the palace

steps.text: Eumaeus went to tell Penelope that her son was safe. Odysseus and Telemachus stayed at the hut, alone together.
There was no sea between them now. There was only one name still waiting to be spoken.

athena.reason: Athena reveals herself to the father before the disguise changes

steps.text: Athena briefly removed the disguise so Telemachus could recognize his father. The young man stepped back in surprise.
“I am your father.”
“My father has been gone all my life.”
“And I have missed all that time.”
They reached for one another. Neither tried to make the years sound smaller than they were.
Father and son planned their return to the palace. They would keep Odysseus’s identity secret until they could face the suitors.
Telemachus would go ahead to the house. Eumaeus would return to guide the disguised Odysseus there the next morning.
“Tomorrow I will enter as the old man again. Let no one see what you know.”
Home was near enough to touch. They would still have to face what had happened inside it.
Athena returned to put the disguise back on Odysseus. Only his son would know who the old traveler really was.
Telemachus left for the palace as they had planned. His father would follow with Eumaeus in the morning.
Eumaeus returned after telling Penelope that her son was safe. He would guide the old traveler to the palace in the morning.
